skill.description: Design and build polished websites and web apps tailored to the brief. Use when creating or redesigning web interfaces, covering layout, color, typography, custom imagery, and motion.

content.user_title: Design Responsive Websites and Web Apps
content.value_statement: Generic layouts can hide the content or controls visitors need first. This skill guides your coding assistant in designing a responsive interface around the brief and reviewing it on desktop and mobile.
actual_capabilities: Derive a visual direction from the subject, audience, and style brief while respecting existing design tokens.
Choose an opening layout that puts content or controls first for tools and reserves prominent hero sections for suitable pages.
Define a type scale, color roles, and navigation hierarchy that fit the project.
Guide the use of project-relative visual assets, including generated imagery when a tool is available.
Specify interface transitions and scroll effects that respect reduced-motion preferences.
Guide desktop and mobile screenshot reviews for overflow, clipping, navigation, and layout collisions.
limitations: The skill provides instructions, not a bundled UI library or starter project.
Custom image generation requires an available image tool. Without one, use supplied assets or code-based visuals.
Rendered visual review requires access to a local preview and browser or screenshot tools.
Contrast and reduced-motion guidance do not replace a full accessibility audit.

use_cases.title: Build a product launch page
use_cases.description: Open with product imagery, explain the primary benefit, and give visitors one clear action.

use_cases.title: Redesign an operations dashboard
use_cases.description: Keep filters and data visible immediately while refining navigation, type hierarchy, and spacing in the existing codebase.

use_cases.title: Review a portfolio before launch
use_cases.description: Inspect the opening screen and project sections at desktop and mobile sizes, then prioritize fixes for overflow and legibility.

prompt_templates.title: Create a simple portfolio
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: Build a new page with images you already have.
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a responsive portfolio for a furniture designer. Use my project photos and give the first screen one clear link to the work.

prompt_templates.title: Refine an existing dashboard
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: Improve an interface without replacing the design system.
prompt_templates.prompt: Redesign this inventory dashboard using its current framework and design tokens. Open directly with the filters and table. Keep labels readable on mobile.

prompt_templates.title: Plan product imagery and motion
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: Design a product page with approved assets and a focused interaction.
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a launch page for this bicycle using the supplied photos. Give the headline clear contrast. Add a product reveal that respects reduced-motion preferences.

prompt_templates.title: Audit and fix a rendered site
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: Review an existing site across viewports before release.
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect the local preview at desktop and 390 by 844 mobile sizes. Review the opening and scrolled sections. Fix clipped headings, navigation collisions, and horizontal overflow without changing approved copy.

output_examples.input: Redesign the opening screen of a support dashboard.
output: The page opens directly with the ticket queue and status filters, without a marketing banner.
Table labels and supporting text use a consistent type scale and clear contrast.

output_examples.input: Build and review a launch page for a desk lamp with supplied photography.
output: A full-width photo shows the lamp behind a readable headline and one purchase action.
The desktop and mobile reviews confirm the heading stays within the viewport and the header does not cover content.

best_practices: Share the audience, primary page action, and existing design constraints before asking for implementation.
Provide approved imagery and copy, and identify text that must remain unchanged.
Review the opening screen and lower sections at desktop and mobile sizes before delivery.
anti_patterns: Place a full-screen marketing banner before a dashboard, documentation page, or utility.
Use decorative badges, fake status cues, or nested cards in place of clear hierarchy.
Guess external image URLs or hardcode paths that only work on one machine.

faq.question: Can I use this skill in an existing project?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance recommends preserving the project's framework and design tokens.

faq.question: Does every page need a hero section?
faq.answer: No. Dashboards, tools, and content indexes should open with the material people came to use.

faq.question: Does the skill generate images on its own?
faq.answer: No. It can direct an available image-generation tool or use supplied assets and code-based visuals.

faq.question: Which screen sizes does the checklist cover?
faq.answer: It calls for desktop views and a 390 by 844 mobile view, including both opening and scrolled sections.

faq.question: Does the checklist verify accessibility compliance?
faq.answer: No. It covers practices such as text contrast and reduced motion, but a separate accessibility review is still needed.

faq.question: Can the skill keep my approved copy unchanged?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide the approved copy as part of the brief. The skill says to preserve user-supplied text verbatim.
